artifacts.synopsis: A minister challenged Presbytery’s procedures and its classification of a transfer candidate’s views on continuing tongues as “not a difference.” The SJC rejected the procedural objections because Presbytery could disregard its committee’s recommendation and had breached no required procedure. It nevertheless held that a difference need not overtly contradict the Standards and that the candidate’s statements implicated WCF 1.1 and 1.6. It annulled the classification and remanded for clarification and a new judgment, without deciding whether the clarified view would be acceptable.

artifacts.synopsis: Philadelphia Presbytery declared that TE Larry Smith's views on continuing prophecy and tongues were not out of accord or hostile to the system of doctrine. Klett et al. complained. The SJC sustained the complaint: Smith's written views affirmed continuing non-general revelation and treated prophecy and tongues as public-worship elements, contrary to WCF 1 and 21, so Presbytery erred under BCO 21-4.f. The SJC annulled Presbytery's May 15, 2021 action. No further action was possible because Smith and his congregation had left the PCA; the matter was concluded, with precedent limited to the written views reviewed.

artifacts.synopsis: The SJC sustained a complaint against Philadelphia Presbytery for failing to judge and record TE Larry Smith’s stated difference over the continuation of prophecy and tongues beyond the apostolic era. The record showed Presbytery approved Smith’s transfer exam and defeated a motion to find his view out of accord, but it did not categorize that view in Smith’s own words. The SJC remanded for a written statement and Presbytery’s categorical judgment, without undoing Smith’s transfer or deciding whether his view was erroneous.

artifacts.title: Webster & Fowler v. Heritage Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Did Heritage Presbytery err by cautioning a session and requesting that it postpone a candidate's election or ordination while a complaint about his qualifications was pending? The SJC said no and denied the complaint. The motion was advice, not an act for or requirement imposed on the session; the session could disregard it, and BCO 43-2 does not bar presbyters from discussing matters related to a complaint not yet before them. The SJC left undecided whether such discussions would disqualify presbyters, since the Ullrey complaint never reached presbytery.

artifacts.title: Aven v. Ohio Valley Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: An SJC complaint alleged that Ohio Valley Presbytery failed to comply with the SJC's prior remand in Case 2014-01, which required it to 'hear further' from TE Charles Hickey about his changed view on Larger Catechism 177. The SJC denied the complaint. It held that the prior decision neither sustained nor denied the original complaint and prescribed no particular examination procedure; Hickey's nine pages of additional affirmations, exegesis, and answers constituted hearing further, and he addressed the five identified areas at least in part. A concurrence believed the SJC could also have adjudicated the confessional-difference merits; a dissent would have found noncompliance and reached the merits.

artifacts.synopsis: Heartland Presbytery granted a transferring OPC teaching elder an exception to WCF 19, judging his stated differences 'more than semantic but not out of accord with any fundamental.' The SJC sustained a complaint not against the merits of that judgment but against the sufficiency of the record supporting it. It held Presbytery clearly erred by failing to develop a sufficient record: the presbyters as a whole did not receive OPCUS's adverse actions, its teaching restriction, or the elder's longer paper. Remanded for those materials and release documentation to be included in the minutes. A concurrence addressed deference; four dissenters found no clear error.

artifacts.title: Aven and Dively v. Ohio Valley Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Two ministers complained that Ohio Valley Presbytery erred by judging TE Charles Hickey's difference with Larger Catechism 177—over restricting the Lord's Supper to those able to examine themselves—as more than semantic but neither hostile to the system nor vital to religion. The SJC neither sustained nor denied the complaint. Because the Record did not sufficiently address Hickey's particular expression and rationale, the Commission remanded to Presbytery for further hearing and a fuller record. It reserved the merits, including whether this formulation of paedocommunion is allowable.

artifacts.synopsis: Pacific Northwest Presbytery adopted a report finding TE Peter Leithart's views not out of accord with the fundamentals of the system of doctrine. The SJC sustained a complaint, holding PNW erred because, without formal judicial process, it lacked authority to declare either that the views were out of accord or that they were not. The record still suggested a strong presumption of guilt. The SJC refused complainants' affirmative declaration and remanded with directions for pastoral counsel under BCO 31-7 and possible BCO 31-2 compliance.
